A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCORE research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, proofs, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original Gaussian, exponential, and AR(1) simulations, plus yeast-screening and clinical-data analyses in Section 6 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical studies and adds a dependence stress test and target-FDR sensitivity experiments in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The SCORE and SCORE+ procedures in Sections 3–5 retain their update rules. V2 Appendix C adds discounted-memory versions of their FDP accounting, introducing decayed discovery totals and modified denominators. This is a limited methodological extension, presented as an outline rather than an implemented, evaluated procedure.

E1.justification: The Gaussian, exponential, AR(1), yeast, and clinical settings are retained. Appendix B.2 adds a distinct adversarial stream in which a null rejection suppresses subsequent alternative signals, deliberately violating CPQD. The target-level sweep reuses existing data-generating settings.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in matched experiments. This includes the e-value families and the six classical p-value comparators: LOND, LORD, SAFFRON, ADDIS, Alpha-investing, and SupLORD. The new checks use existing SCORE/SCORE+ procedures.

E3.justification: V2 adds pointwise power ratios relative to each family's baseline and a sensitivity sweep over alpha = 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, and 0.20. The new stress-test protocol specifies alternating null/non-null hypotheses and a rejection-triggered signal trap. Previously reported main-experiment settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds two substantive investigations absent from v1: a CPQD-violation stress test examining SCORE+ failure versus basic SCORE control, and target-FDR sensitivity analyses across both main simulation settings. These substantially expand evidence about robustness and applicability; relocating the existing FDR plots is a separate presentation change.

E5.justification: Both versions report 500 repetitions for the main simulations and 500 random splits for the clinical analysis, whose error-bar display is retained. The new sensitivity tables use the same 500-repetition averaging practice. No new seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Figure 9 newly shows SCORE+-LORD and SCORE+-SAFFRON reaching FDR approximately 0.077 and 0.065 against a 0.05 target under the stress scenario. Tables 2–3 add sensitivity results and power ratios. Main simulation curves have small numerical updates while preserving their ordering; Table 1's yeast counts and the earlier AR(1) and clinical plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds a limited formal generalization: discounted discovery counts, memory-FDR estimators, a predictable-denominator derivation, and a corresponding CPQD requirement for retroactive accounting. The core theorems remain unchanged. The rewritten independence/PQD proof preserves its existing argument, and the memory extension is not presented as a fully proved new theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same dominance and finite-sample FDR contributions. The conclusion newly asserts compatibility with decaying-memory FDR, supported by Appendix C's outline. Section 2 also removes the stronger phrase 'regardless of the stopping time' from the stated control objective.

C2.justification: V2 adds specific qualifications about limited gains with uniformly weak or very strong evidence, interprets the CPQD-violating failure scenario, and explains why shared clinical calibration data do not automatically justify SCORE+. These clarify applicability boundaries without replacing the central interpretation of overshoot refunds.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 supplies an explicit construction recipe for the new stress stream. V2 also adds a direct clinical-dataset access URL to the Golovenkin et al. reference. Existing implementation parameters and data-processing descriptions are largely retained.

R1.justification: The cited-work set is retained. Section 4.4 adds explicit positioning of e-LOND, e-LORD, and e-SAFFRON as canonical available procedures and characterizes SCORE's applicability through the standard indicator bound. Appendix C additionally connects the extension directly to Ramdas et al.'s decaying-memory criterion.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. V2 adds a p-value/e-value calibration explanation, refines the CPQD discussion and one proof, and adds publication disclosures. References move before the appendices, while the former Appendices B–D become D–F following the inserted material.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column conference main text and extensively reorganizes the simulation displays. Combined plots become family-specific power and power-ratio figures, with FDR trajectories displayed separately in the appendix. A stress-test figure and two sensitivity tables are added; earlier appendix charts are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the CPQD failure test and target-level sensitivity checks provide useful evidence about when the procedures work. Clearer applicability qualifications, redesigned comparisons, and a dataset link improve assessment and usability. The central contribution and most existing evidence remain intact, while the memory extension is only outlined, so the overall quality gain is limited.
